rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise points back to God's prior favor in bringing Joseph near the king and rescuing him from prison's distress.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم يعني به ومثل ذلك الإنعام الذي أنعمنا عليه في تقريبنا إياه من قلب الملك وإنجائنا إياه من غم الحبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To empower Joseph in the land means enabling him to do what he wished by removing obstacles.
rows.anchor: أي أقدرناه على ما يريد برفع الموانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb يتبوأ is an accusative circumstantial expression; Ibn Kathir reads نشاء with a divine ن, while the other readers use ياء referring to Joseph.
rows.anchor: يتبوأ في موضع نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's unrestricted settling means no one could oppose or contest him; he independently controlled whatever he wished.
rows.anchor: بل صار مستقلا بكل ما شاء وأراد ثم بين تعالى ما يؤكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated attribution of Joseph's dominion to God means the kingdom itself came from God, as the wording and decisive proof require; al-Qadi's metaphorical account is rejected.
rows.anchor: وجوابه : أنا ندعي أن نفس تلك المملكة إنما حصلت من قبل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says the kingdom resulted from God's actions in its contributing circumstances, so it is as if it came from God.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : تلك المملكة لما لم تتم إلا بالأمور فعلها الله تعالى

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi reads the verse as saying God orders the bestowal of blessings according to what serves people's welfare.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : هذه الآية تدل على أنه تعالى يجري أمر نعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse assigns blessings to God's unconditioned will and power; the qualification of welfare is imposed by al-Qadi and absent from its wording.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن الأمور معلقة بالمشيئة الإلهية والقدرة المحضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot waste reward because loss would arise from incapacity, ignorance, or miserliness, all impossible of God.
rows.anchor: إضاعة الأجر إما أن يكون للعجز أو للجهل أو للبخل والكل ممتنع في حق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's calling Joseph a doer of good refutes the claim that he lay between the woman's legs: that claim either makes God's judgment false or is itself false.
rows.anchor: ولو صدق القول / بأنه جلس بين شعبها الأربع لامتنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes خير comparatively: Joseph's afterlife reward exceeds his high worldly station because it benefits purely, lasts, and comes with honor.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : المراد منه أن يوسف عليه السلام وإن كان قد وصل إلى المنازل العالية والدرجات الرفيعة في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading takes خير as good in itself, as in saying stew is a good bestowed through God's kindness, without comparison.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أن لفظ الخير قد يستعمل لكون أحد الخيرين أفضل من الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the comparative reading, worldly pleasures must also count as good; on the intrinsic-good reading, the verse may treat afterlife good as the only true good and other things as futile.
rows.anchor: إن حملناه على الوجه الأول لزم أن تكون ملاذ الدنيا موصوفة بالخيرية أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise specifically describes Joseph as a believer and God-fearing person, affirming his piety at the earlier temptation; God also calls him a doer of good and sincere servant, against the claim he was a grave sinner.
rows.anchor: فكان هذا شهادة من الله تعالى على أنه عليه السلام كان في ذلك الوقت من المتقين

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues that the promise to the God-fearing refutes Murji'ites who expect afterlife reward even for people who do not avoid major sins.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : قوله تعالى : { ولاجر الاخرة خير للذين ءامنوا وكانوا يتقون } يدل على بطلان قول المرجئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the argument is weak: comparative خير makes the pious' reward better, not exclusive, while the basic-good reading promises good to the pious without denying it to others.
rows.anchor: قلنا : هذا ضعيف ، لأنا إن حملنا لفظ خير على أفعل التفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When famine reached Jacob's town, he sent ten sons to Egypt to buy food from a righteous man; the journey reunited Joseph with them and fulfilled the prediction made when they cast him into the well.
rows.anchor: لما عم القحط في البلاد ، ووصل أيضا إلى البلدة التي كان يسكنها يعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph recognized them because God's prediction and his dream led him to expect their arrival, so he scrutinized travelers from distant places and learned their identities.
rows.anchor: وأيضا الرؤيا التي رآها كانت دليلا على أنهم يصلون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They failed to recognize Joseph because he kept them at a distance and spoke through intermediaries; royal awe and their need also prevented close scrutiny.
rows.anchor: أمر حجابه بأن يوقفوهم من البعد وما كان يتكلم معهم إلا بالواسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had last seen him as a child and now saw a bearded ruler in changed dress and royal ornaments; forty years had passed and they had forgotten the episode.
rows.anchor: فيقال : إن من وقت ما ألقوه في الجب إلى هذا الوقت كان قد مضى أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may have withheld recognition from their hearts to fulfill the prediction that they would not perceive Joseph, making this a miracle of his.
rows.anchor: لعله تعالى ما خلق ذلك العرفان والتذكير في قلوبهم تحقيقا لما أخبره عنه

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines furnishing travelers as preparing what they need for the journey; the term also covers a bride's or dead person's necessary equipment.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : جهزت القوم تجهيزا إذا تكلفت لهم جهازهم للسفر

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says all Qur'an readers use the fatḥa in جِهاز, while the kasra is a poor dialect.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري : القراء كلهم على فتح الجيم ، والكسر لغة ليست بجيدة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say Joseph gave each brother a camel-load and generously hosted them and supplied their travel needs.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : حمل لكل رجل منهم بعيرا وأكرمهم أيضا بالنزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most fitting prompt was that Joseph normally gave one camel-load per person; when the ten explained that their elderly father and remaining brother also needed food, he sent two extra loads and asked to see the favored brother.
rows.anchor: الوجه الأول : وهو أحسنها إن عادة يوسف عليه السلام مع الكل

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Another account says Joseph suspected them of spying, asked who they were, and required one brother to stay as hostage while they brought their brother; the lot selected Simeon, who had treated Joseph best.
rows.anchor: قالوا معاذ الله نحن إخوة بنو أب واحد شيخ صديق نبي اسمه يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possible prompt is that Joseph questioned why their father was alone; after they explained he kept one son because he loved him most, Joseph inferred that this brother must excel even them and wished to meet him.
rows.anchor: لأجل نقص في جسده ؟ فقالوا : لا . بل لأجل أنه يحبه أكثر من محبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suspicion-of-spies account is unlikely: it conflicts with Joseph's warm assurance that he completed their measure and was a good host, and a truthful prophet would not falsely accuse people he knew were innocent.
rows.anchor: هذا الكلام يضعف الوجه الثاني وهو الذي نقلناه عن المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أوفي الكيل means completing the measure without shortchanging; Joseph adds a camel-load for their brother, and خير المنزلين means best of hosts.
rows.anchor: وأزيدكم حمل بعير آخر لأجل أخيكم ، وأنا خير المنزلين ، أي خير المضيفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph combines inducement in his generous measure and hospitality with a threat to deny food and access; their famine made this a severe warning because they could obtain food only from him.
rows.anchor: جمع بين الترغيب والترهيب . أما الترغيب : فهو قوله : { ألا ترون أنى أوفى الكيل وأنا خير المنزلين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to try to persuade their father and repeat their pledge for emphasis; alternatively, they mean they will bring the brother or do everything within their power.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون { وإنا لفاعلون } أن نجيئك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read لفتيانه with alif and nun; the other readers have لفتيته without them. Abu Ali al-Farisi explains the pair as plural forms for smaller and larger numbers.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم لفتيانه بالألف والنون

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says فتية is a small-number plural and فتيان a large-number plural; few attendants suit keeping the secret, while many suit the plural رحال.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي الفتية جمع فتى في العدد القليل والفتيان للكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators say the brothers did not know Joseph returned their money; the contrary view is weak because his hope that they would recognize it presupposes their ignorance.
rows.anchor: اتفق الأكثرون على أن إخوة يوسف ما كانوا عالمين بجعل البضاعة في رحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that discovering the returned money would reveal Joseph's generosity and motivate them to return and trade with him.
rows.anchor: علموا أن ذلك كان كرما من يوسف وسخاء محضا فيبعثهم ذلك على العود إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Joseph feared their father lacked the money for another journey.
rows.anchor: خاف أن لا يكون عند أبيه من الورق ما يرجعون به مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that he meant to relieve his father during the famine.
rows.anchor: أراد به التوسعة على أبيه لأن الزمان كان زمان القحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation is that taking payment from his needy father and brothers for food would be mean.
rows.anchor: رأى أن أخذ ثمن الطعام من أبيه وإخوته مع شدة حاجتهم إلى الطعام لؤم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says they might think the money had accidentally ended up in their bags and return either to learn why or to restore it to its owner.
rows.anchor: الخامس : قال الفراء : إنهم متى شاهدوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that Joseph wanted to help them privately, without making them feel shame or indebtedness.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يحسن إليهم على وجه لا يلحقهم به عيب ولا منة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have wanted them to know that his request for their brother was neither to harm him nor to charge them more.
rows.anchor: السابع : مقصوده أن يعرفوا أنه لا يطلب ذلك الأخ لأجل الإيذاء والظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He could show their father that he sought the brother to honor him, so the request would not burden the father.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يعرف أبوه أنه أكرمهم وطلبه له لمزيد الإكرام فلا يثقل على أبيه إرسال أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have hidden the money in their bags to protect it from highway robbers until they reached their father during the famine.
rows.anchor: وكان يخاف اللصوص من قطع الطريق ، فوضع تلك الدراهم في رحالهم حتى تبقى مخفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final explanation is that Joseph answered their great wrong with still greater kindness.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يقابل مبالغتهم في الإساءة بمبالغته في الإحسان إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that the ration was withheld may refer to the food they had requested for their father and brother, which was denied.
rows.anchor: أنهم لما طلبوا الطعام لأبيهم وللأخ الباقي عنده منعوا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they mean that future rations will be denied unless they bring their brother, echoing Joseph's threat.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه منع الكيل في المستقبل وهو إشارة إلى قول يوسف : { فإن لم تأتونى به فلا كيل لكم عندى } ( يوسف : 60 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read يكتل, supporting the first explanation; the rest read نكتل, supporting the second.
rows.anchor: والقراءة الأولى تقوى القول الأول ، والقراءة الثانية تقوي القول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob recalls that they made the same promise to protect Joseph, so their repeated assurance about Benjamin offers no new basis for trust.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنكم ذكرتم قبل هذا الكلام في يوسف وضمنتم لي حفظه حيث قلتم : { وإنا له لحافظون } ( يوسف : 12 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read حافظا with tanwin as a specification or circumstantial expression, meaning God is a better preserver for you; the others read it as a verbal noun, God's protection being better than yours.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي { حافظا } بالألف على التمييز والتفسير

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash reads فالله خير حافظا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش { فالله خير حافظا }

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra's reading includes خير حافظا وهو أرحم الراحمين.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه { خير * حافظا وهو أرحم الرحمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob may mean that he trusted them over Joseph and saw what happened, so he now entrusts Benjamin's protection to God.
rows.anchor: وثقت بكم في حفظ يوسف عليه السلام فكان ما كان فالآن أتوكل على الله في حفظ بنيامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob may send Benjamin because the brothers have matured toward goodness, show less jealousy of Benjamin, and famine makes the trip necessary; perhaps God revealed and guaranteed his safe return.
rows.anchor: كبروا ومالوا إلى الخير والصلاح

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most scholars take Jacob's words to show that he permitted Benjamin to leave with them.
rows.anchor: قلنا : الأكثرون قالوا : يدل عليه

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say the statement does not prove permission: it may mean that if Jacob allowed the trip, Benjamin would be protected by God rather than them, or refer to Joseph, whom Jacob knew was alive.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : لا يدل عليه ، وفيه وجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متاع generally means anything usable for enjoyment; here it may mean the food they carried or its containers.
rows.anchor: المتاع ما يصلح لأن يستمتع به وهو عام في كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce ردت with a damma on ra; Alqama reads it with kasra. Al-Zamakhshari explains the kasra as transferred from the doubled dal, like قيل and بيع; Qutrub gives a similar transfer in another phrase.
rows.anchor: واختلف القراء في { ردت } فالأكثرون بضم الراء ، وقرأ علقمة بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ما is negative, they may mean they told no lie in praising Joseph's extraordinary kindness.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : أنها للنفي ، وعلى هذا التقدير ففيه وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the negative reading, they may mean Joseph's kindness could not be exceeded, since he returned their money after giving them food.
rows.anchor: أنه بلغ في الإكرام إلى غاية ما وراءها شيء آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the negative reading, their returned money suffices to pay for the next journey, so they need no further goods from their father.
rows.anchor: لا نبغي منك عند رجوعنا إليه بضاعة أخرى ، فإن هذه التي معنا كافية لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ما is interrogative, they ask what more they could want after receiving food and getting their payment back so graciously.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن كلمة ( ما ) ههنا للاستفهام ، والمعنى : لما رأوا أنه رد إليهم بضاعتهم

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i says ماره يميره ميرا means bringing someone provisions, especially food.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي : يقال ماره يميره ميرا إذا أتاه بميرة أي بطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Joseph measured one camel-load for each person, their brother's presence should earn one additional load.
rows.anchor: معناه : أن يوسف عليه السلام كان يكيل لكل رجل حمل بعير

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil, followed by al-Zajjaj, says the small measure is easy for this generous man who eagerly gives freely.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : ذلك كيل يسير على هذا الرجل المحسن لسخائه وحرصه على البذل وهو اختيار الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading calls the measure brief: a short wait should not be prolonged by detention or delay.
rows.anchor: والثاني : ذلك كيل يسير ، أي قصير المدة ليس سبيل مثله أن تطول مدته بسبب الحبس والتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading says the ration without their brother is small, so they should send him to exchange scarcity for abundance.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد ذلك الذي يدفع إلينا دون أخينا شيء يسير قليل فابعث أخانا معنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: موثق is a covenant one can rely on, expressed as a verbal noun with the sense of a passive participle; من الله means reinforced by invoking and swearing by God.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن الموثق مصدر بمعنى الثقة ومعناه : العهد الذي يوثق به فهو مصدر بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لتأتنني emphasizes the oath: Jacob requires them to swear by God that they will bring Benjamin back.
rows.anchor: دخلت اللام ههنا لأجل أنا بينا أن المراد بالموثق من الله اليمين

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the exception as connected: the promise is phrased affirmatively but means they will not fail to bring him except under one unavoidable cause.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : هذا الاستثناء متصل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets being surrounded as all of them dying, an excuse; Arabic idiom describes someone near death as surrounded, as in the stories of the garden and storm.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : إلا أن تموتوا كلكم فيكون ذلك عذرا عندي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets being surrounded as becoming defeated and overpowered so that they cannot return.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : ما ذكره قتادة { إلا أن يحاط بكم } إلا أن تصيروا مغلوبين مقهورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here God is a witness entrusted with the covenant: keeping it earns reward, while betrayal incurs punishment.
rows.anchor: يريد شهيد ، لأن الشهيد وكيل بمعنى أنه موكول إليه هذا العهد

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Most commentators say Jacob told his handsome, numerous sons to enter by separate gates because he feared the evil eye.
rows.anchor: قول جمهور المفسرين أنه خاف من العين عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi adduces the early exegetes' agreement and several Prophetic reports as proof that the evil eye is real.
rows.anchor: إطباق المتقدمين من المفسرين على أن المراد من هذه الآية ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet sought God's protection for Hasan and Husayn from devils, harmful creatures, and the evil eye, saying Abraham used the same prayer for Ishmael and Isaac.
rows.anchor: ما روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعوذ الحسن والحسين فيقول : ( أعيذ كما بكلمات الله التامة

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: Ubada reports that the Prophet was ill, then well after Gabriel recited an invocation for protection from harm, the evil eye, and envy.
rows.anchor: ما روى عبادة بن الصامت قال : دخلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في أول النهار

rows.speaker: أسماء
rows.claim: Asma said Ja'far's fair-skinned sons were especially vulnerable to the evil eye and asked the Prophet whether she should seek a protective recitation; he agreed.
rows.anchor: الرابع : روي أن بني جعفر ابن أبي طالب كانوا غلمنا بيضا فقالت أسماء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When Umm Salama's child was ill, people said the child had been struck by the evil eye; the Prophet asked why they did not seek a protective recitation.
rows.anchor: دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت أم سلمة وعندها صبي يشتكي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said the evil eye is real and, if anything could precede destiny, it would be the evil eye.
rows.anchor: العين حق ولو كان شيء يسبق القدر لسبقت العين القدر

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the Prophet would tell the person who caused the evil eye to perform ablution, then wash the affected person with that water.
rows.anchor: والسابع : قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها : كن يأمر العائن أن يتوضأ ثم يغسل منه المعين

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Jubba'i emphatically denies that the evil eye exists but offers no argument, much less a proof.
rows.anchor: أن أبا علي الجبائي أنكر هذا المعنى إنكارا بليغا ولم يذكر في إنكاره شبهة فضلا عن حجة

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Al-Hafiz proposes that rays extend from the eye to an admired person and affect them like a sting, poison, or fire.
rows.anchor: الأول : قال الحافظ : إنه يمتد من العين أجزاء فتصل بالشخص المستحسن

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi objects that this theory should affect an unadmired person just as much as an admired one.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وهذا ضعيف لأنه لو كان الأمر كما قال ، لوجب أن يؤثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that admiration can produce fearful attachment to a cherished possession or envy and grief at an enemy's blessing; either concentrates and heats the spirit, strengthening the eye's ray, unlike mere sight.
rows.anchor: عند الاستحسان القوي تسخن الروح جدا فيسخن شعاع العين بخلاف ما إذا لم يستحسن

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abu Hashim and al-Balkhi say the evil eye may be real because a person captivated by admiration may, as a matter of divine wisdom, have the admired object changed to loosen that attachment; remembering God and seeking refuge may avert it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هاشم وأبو القاسم البلخي إنه لا يمتنع أن تكون العين حقا

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The philosophers argue that causes need not work through perceptible heat, cold, moisture, or dryness: fear can make a person fall from a plank, and imagining an enemy can heat the body, showing mental states can alter bodies.
rows.anchor: قالوا هذا الكلام مبني على مقدمة وهي أنه ليس من شرط المؤثر أن يكون تأثيره بحسب هذه الكيفيات المحسوسة

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: Since minds initiate bodily movement and souls differ in kind, some souls may affect another body when they see and admire it; longstanding experience and prophetic testimony confirm the possibility.
rows.anchor: فلما ثبت أن تصور النفس يوجب تغير بدنه الخاص لم يبعد أيضا أن يكون بعض النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi accepts the early commentators' evil-eye interpretation because it is rationally possible and they unanimously hold it.
rows.anchor: الذي أطبق عليه المتقدمون من المفسرين في تفسير هذه الآية بإصابة العين كلام حق لا يمكن رده

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i offers an alternative: the brothers' beauty and fame might provoke Egyptian envy or make the king fear them as a threat and imprison them.
rows.anchor: أن أبناء يعقوب اشتهروا بمصر وتحدث الناس بهم وبحسهم وكمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the fame-and-envy explanation is possible, but the evil-eye account is preferable because it is not irrational and most commentators adopt it.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا الوجه محتمل لا إنكار فيه إلا أن القول الأول قد بينا أنه لا امتناع فيه بحسب العقل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Jacob first feared the evil eye, then returned to the knowledge that nothing can avert God's decree and recognized the eye as powerless.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن الحسن أنه قال : خاف عليهم العين ، فقال : { لا تدخلوا من باب واحد } ثم رجع إلى علمه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads the passage as referring to the evil eye and says God's power to repel its effect is consistent with Jacob's statement that nothing avails against God.
rows.anchor: وكان قتادة يفسر الآية بإصابة العين ويقول : ليس في قوله : { وما أغنى عنكم من الله من شىء } إبطال له

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i says Jacob knew Egypt's king was Joseph but could not reveal it by God's command; he split the brothers up to bring Benjamin to Joseph privately.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول إبراهيم النخعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's precaution follows ordinary means, while his denial of its ultimate power affirms that outcomes occur only by God's decree; people must strive and avoid harm while knowing caution cannot defeat destiny.
rows.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى رعاية الأسباب المعتبرة في هذا العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حكم means binding and preventing the contrary, like a rein that restrains an animal; judgment makes one possible outcome prevail so the other cannot occur.
rows.anchor: لأن الحكم عبارة عن الإلزام والمنع من النقيض وسميت حكمة الدابة بهذا الاسم ، لأنها تمنع الدابة عن الحركات الفاسدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because only God exercises judgment in that sense, every possibility depends on His decree, power, will, and judgment, directly or through an intermediary.
rows.anchor: فبين تعالى أن الحكم بهذا التفسير ليس إلا لله سبحانه وتعالى ، وذلك يدل على أن جميع الممكنات مستندة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since all good and relief from harm come from God, trust and desire belong to Him alone; Razi points readers to al-Ghazali's chapter on trust for a fuller account.
rows.anchor: فلزم القطع بأن حصول كل الخيرات ودفع كل الآفات من الله ، ويوجب أنه لا توكل إلا على الله

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say God confirms Jacob's statement: entering separately could not shield them from God's decree.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : لما قال يعقوب : { وما أغنى عنكم من الله من شىء } ( يوسف : 67 ) صدقه الله في ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says separating could neither repel God's decree nor alter what He had ordained.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ذلك التفرق ما كان يرد قضاء الله ولا أمرا قدره الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says a destined evil eye would strike them whether they were together or apart.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : إن العين لو قدر أن تصيبهم لأصابتهم وهم متفرقون كما تصيبهم وهم مجتمعون

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says that if their destruction together by the evil eye were decreed, separating would be no different from gathering.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : لو سبق في علم الله أن العين تهلكهم عند الاجتماع لكان تفرقهم كاجتماعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من شيء can be accusative as the object—nothing was removed from God's decree—or nominative as the subject—nothing could benefit them alongside His decree.
rows.anchor: قوله : { من شىء } يحتمل النصب بالمفعولية والرفع بالفاعلية

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls the exception for Jacob's inner need disconnected: their separate entry fulfilled his wish; proposed wishes include fear of the evil eye, Egyptian envy or royal harm, and fear they would not return.
rows.anchor: فقال الزجاج : إنه استثناء منقطع ، والمعنى : لكن حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reads ما as a verbal noun or relative pronoun: Jacob knows through God's teaching, or knows the thing God taught him.
rows.anchor: فقال الواحدي : يحتمل أن يكون { ما } مصدرية والهاء عائدة إلى يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings take Jacob's knowledge as careful preservation of what he learned, or knowledge of its benefits and effects that he puts into practice.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية قولان آخران : الأول : أن المراد بالعلم الحفظ ، أي أنه لذو حفظ لما علمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people may fail to know what Jacob knows, or fail to recognize his knowledge; the reference is to polytheists unaware of God's useful guidance to His allies.
rows.anchor: وفيه وجهان : الأول : ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون مثل ما علم يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph seated the brothers in pairs; Benjamin, left alone, mourned that his brother would have sat with him, so Joseph invited him to share his table and then arranged to lodge with him alone.
rows.anchor: بقي بنيامين وحده فبكى وقال لو كان أخي يوسف حيا لأجلسني معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph drew Benjamin close by lodging him where he himself would stay.
rows.anchor: أي أنزله في الموضع الذي كان يأوي إليه

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says إني أنا أخوك means Joseph would fill the role of brotherly companionship, not claim shared lineage.
rows.anchor: قال وهب : لم يرد أنه أخوه من النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the literal kinship reading: it better removes loneliness and the ordinary meaning should not be abandoned without necessity.
rows.anchor: والصحيح ما عليه سائر المفسرين من أنه أراد تعريف النسب

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Linguists derive تبتئس from distress and hardship; it means bringing grief and misery upon oneself.
rows.anchor: فقال أهل اللغة : تبتئس تفتعل من البؤس وهو الضرر والشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Benjamin should not grieve over the brothers' continuing envy and effort to turn their father's affection away.
rows.anchor: المراد بما كانوا يعملون من إقامتهم على حسدنا والحرص على انصراف وجه أبينا عنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Joseph, now free of hostility, wanted Benjamin likewise to let go of their brothers' past misdeeds.
rows.anchor: ما بقي في قلبه شيء من العداوة وصار صافيا مع إخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Benjamin might fear that the brothers would envy the king's special favor toward him as they had envied Joseph; Joseph reassures him that God reunited them.
rows.anchor: فأمنه منه وقال : لا تلتفت إلى ذلك فإن الله قد جمع بيني وبينك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi, from Ibn Abbas, says the brothers mocked Joseph and Benjamin because their maternal grandfather worshipped idols and Joseph's mother had taken his idol chest hoping to end that worship.
rows.anchor: الرابع : روى الكلبي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أن إخوة يوسف عليه السلام كانوا يعيرون يوسف وأخاه

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf says the siqaya was a drinking vessel, the suwa'; one account says the king drank from it before it became a measuring cup, but Razi considers that unlikely for a king's large cup.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : مشربة يسقي بها وهو الصواع

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: A closer account says the vessel served both to water animals and measure grain; reports that it was silver gilt, gold, or jewel-encrusted are unlikely, so Razi prefers a valuable but ordinary vessel.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانت الدواب تسقى بها ويكال بها أيضا وهذا أقرب

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says أذّن can mean repeated informing because the form implies repetition; it may also be a single announcement, since Arabs use it like أفعل.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : أذن معناه أعلم إعلاما بعد إعلام لأن فعل يوجب تكرير الفعل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says أذنت and أذنت both mean informed, without distinction; تأذين is a loud announcement.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه : أذنت وأذنت معناه أعلمت لا فرق بينهما

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham says عير can mean a caravan of camels, donkeys, or mules; the restriction to camels alone is false.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم : كل ما سير عليه من الإبل والحمير والبغال فهو عير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations restrict عير to loaded camels because they travel back and forth, or to donkey caravans; usage later extended it to any caravan.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي قافلة الحمير ، ثم كثر ذلك حتى قيل لكل قافلة عير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the caravan means addressing its people, as in the expression O God's cavalry, ride.
rows.anchor: المراد أصحاب العير كقوله : يا خيل الله اركبي

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads وجعل السقاية, treating the clause as completing what happened before the herald waited until they had departed to call out.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : { وجعل * السقاية } على حذف جواب لما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Joseph arranged the accusation after privately telling Benjamin the plan and obtaining his consent; this would spare him distress and avoid sin.
rows.anchor: لما أظهر لأخيه أنه يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that they meant the brothers had stolen Joseph from their father, using an indirect accusation.
rows.anchor: أن المراد إنكم لسارقون يوسف من أبيه إلا أنهم ما أظهروا هذا الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer is that the herald spoke as a question, not a false assertion.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك المؤذن ربما ذكر ذلك النداء على سبيل الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the text never says Joseph ordered the call; most plausibly his men made the accusation themselves after the cup was missing and no one else was present.
rows.anchor: والأقرب إلى ظاهر الحال أنهم فعلوا ذلك من أنفسهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reads تفقدون from أفقدته, meaning to find something lost.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي { تفقدون } من أفقدته إذا وجدته فقيدا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf records forms صواع, صاع, صوع, and صوع, with variation in the vowels of ṣād and the spelling of ʿayn.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : قرىء صواع وصاع وصوع وصوع بفتح الصاد وضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians derive plural صيعان from صواع and أصواع from صاع; others say صاع and صواع are equivalent, citing Abu Hurayra's reading.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم جمع صواع صيعان ، كغراب وغربان ، وجمع صاع أصواع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view distinguishes the words: صواع names the object while سقاية describes its use, like a cup versus a water-skin.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الصواع اسم ، والسقاية وصف ، كقولهم : كوز وسقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised load is food, and زعيم means guarantor; Mujahid identifies the guarantor as the herald, al-Kalbi notes the Yemeni dialect, and Abu Ubayda reports al-Kisa'i's idiom for guaranteeing.
rows.anchor: ولمن جاء به حمل بعير } أي من الطعام { أنا * به زعيم } قال مجاهد : الزعيم هو المؤذن الذي أذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that surety was valid in their law, and the Prophet also ruled that a guarantor is liable.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على أن الكفالة كانت صحيحة في شرعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A camel-load of food was a known quantity, so the guarantee was sufficiently determinate; although it guaranteed return of stolen property before liability was due, their law may have allowed it.
rows.anchor: قلنا : حمل بعير من الطعام كان معلوما عندهم ، فصحت الكفالة به إلا أن هذه الكفالة مال لرد سرقة

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basran grammarians say wāw in والله replaced tā, itself a substitute for wāw; tā is restricted to God's name because it inflects weakly elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قال البصريون : الواو في { والله } بدل من التاء والتاء بدل من الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers swore they had not come to corrupt the land; their restraint from taking property, even muzzling their animals to protect crops, and their worship made corruption implausible.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : حلفوا على أمرين : أحدهما : على أنهم ما جاؤا لأجل الفساد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also deny theft because they brought their own money back from Egypt rather than appropriating it when they found it in their packs.
rows.anchor: لما وجدوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم حملوها من بلادهم إلى مصر ولم يستحلوا أخذها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says their law enslaved a thief for the theft, analogous to the amputation penalty in Islamic law; the person found with the stolen item himself becomes the penalty.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس كانوا في ذلك الزمان يستعبدون كل سارق بسرقته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives two parses: either the person found with the item is the penalty and the rest explains it, or the whole clause is the predicate with an emphatic implicit himself.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : وفيه وجهان : أحدهما : أن يقال جزاؤه مبتدأ ومن وجد في رحله خبره

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: The grammarians cite a verse repeating الموت to illustrate emphatic restatement in the clause's construction.
rows.anchor: وأنشد النحويون : لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء … نغص الموت الغني والفقيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like this punishment means that wrongdoers who steal are enslaved; the phrase may belong to Joseph's brothers or be the Egyptian officers' response to their proposal.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل : هذا من بقية كلام أخوة يوسف . وقيل : إنهم لما قالوا جزاؤه من وجد في رحله فهو جزاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the brothers accepted enslavement as the penalty, the herald took them for a search; Joseph searched their bags before Benjamin's to remove suspicion, and containers are vessels enclosing their contents.
rows.anchor: قبل وعاء أخيه } لإزالة التهمة والأوعية جمع الوعاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads وعاء with a ḍamma on its wāw, a dialect form; Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads من أخيه, changing the wāw to hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن { وعاء أخيه } بضم الواو وهي لغة ، وقرأ سعيد بن جبير { من أخيه } فقلب الواو همزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun for the cup alternates between feminine and masculine because feminine refers to سقاية and masculine to صواع, because صواع accepts both genders, or because Joseph and his servants used different names.
rows.anchor: قالوا رجع ضمير المؤنث إلى السقاية وضمير المذكر إلى الصواع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Joseph sought God's forgiveness as he searched each bag for having accused them; when only Benjamin remained he said the boy seemed innocent, but the brothers insisted he be searched too.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال : كان لا ينظر في وعاء إلا استغفر الله تائبا مما قذفهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine devising refers to using the brothers' own rule that a thief be enslaved; divine words of plotting describe the unavoidable outcome, not an improper initial deception.
rows.anchor: المعنى ومثل ذلك الكيد كدنا ليوسف ، وذلك إشارة إلى الحكم باسترقاق السارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Words like كيد are applied to God by their final result, not their initial motive: here it means bringing someone unknowingly into an unavoidable hardship; Razi cites the discussion of 2:26.
rows.anchor: أمثال هذه الألفاظ تحمل على نهايات الأغراض لا على بدايات الأغراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God supported Joseph and raised his cause after his brothers had tried to thwart him.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : المراد أن إخوة يوسف سعوا في إبطال أمر يوسف ، والله تعالى نصره وقواه وأعلى أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God inspired the brothers to declare enslavement the penalty, allowing Joseph to keep Benjamin when the cup appeared in his bag.
rows.anchor: ألقى في قلوب إخوته أن حكموا بأن جزاء السارق هو أن يسترق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptian law required a thief to be beaten and pay twice the stolen value, so Joseph could not detain Benjamin under it; God's plan let him retain Benjamin by the brothers' own rule of enslavement.
rows.anchor: كان حكم الملك في السارق أن يضرب ويغرم ضعفي ما سرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, Asim, and al-Kisa'i read درجات without annexation, while the others annex it.
rows.anchor: المسألة الأولى : قرأ حمزة وعاصم والكسائي { درجات } بالتنوين غير مضاف ، والباقون بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raises whom He wills by guiding them to ways of attaining their aims and granting kinds of knowledge and virtue; here Joseph is raised above his brothers in every respect.
rows.anchor: هو أنه تعالى رفع درجات يوسف على إخوته في كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shows knowledge is the noblest station: God praises Joseph's insight in this plan, and similarly praises Abraham's reasoning against the divinity of celestial bodies, though their ranks differ greatly.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن العلم أشرف المقامات وأعلى الدرجات

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that God knows through His essence, not an attribute of knowledge: otherwise He would be a possessor of knowledge with a knower above Him under the verse's general wording.
rows.anchor: احتجوا بهذه الآية على أنه تعالى عالم بذاته لا بالعلم

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The Ash'aris cite verses affirming God's knowledge; Razi limits above every knower to Joseph and his brothers, since the derivative knower cannot exist without the simple source knowledge, so the general wording must be specified.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أصحابنا قالوا دلت سائر الآيات على إثبات العلم لله تعالى
